# Regression gate

<!-- Generated by scripts/run_regression_gate.py; do not edit by hand. -->

The 71 contract-benchmark cases read as a pull-request gate. The contract was pinned when the fixed function landed. A later change either turns the function back into the buggy version (a regression the gate should block) or keeps the fix (a change the gate should let through). An unresolved answer sends the change to a human. Values are medians over runs, with the range in brackets; see [RESULTS.md](RESULTS.md) for the per-case answers. The mumei + LLM port row is post-fidelity-gate: a raw verifier proof that fails port fidelity evidence is unresolved rather than a passed regression.

## Unresolved outcome taxonomy

Regressions let through are false acceptance and good changes blocked are false positives. The unresolved outcomes below are mutually exclusive per checked change; medians use the same run aggregation as the gate table. Subtype medians are aggregated independently, so they need not sum to the unresolved-count median when the subtype alternates across runs. Unsupported means the input, generated port or verifier capability cannot represent the case; inconclusive means no evidence either way; environment failure means tool or transport failure; budget exhausted means the declared timeout was consumed.

## Verification measurement

Model and verifier measurements are totals over the recorded runs. Model time sums the seconds in usage-recorded provider responses; retry backoff and failed provider attempts stay outside that model-time measurement. Verification time and declared timeout budget cover recorded outcome-determining verifier calls, including vacuity controls, fidelity replay, output equivalence and per-call input/output glue inside `verify_text`; certificate emission/rechecks, gate orchestration and report rendering are outside. Historical rows expose measured-versus-expected call coverage instead of looking fully instrumented.

| Gate | Model | Model time | Verification time | Verification budget |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| mumei (hand-written ports) | — | — | — / 0 of 213 calls | — / 0 of 213 calls |
| mumei + LLM port | openai/gpt-6-luna | 2896.1s | 35.3s / 734 of 1160 calls | 22020.0s / 734 of 1160 calls |
| LLM review | openai/gpt-6-luna | 1876.1s | — | — |

How to read it:

- **mumei (hand-written ports)** is the gate once a port exists for the function. The ports were written with knowledge of the defects, so this row shows what the pinned contracts can enforce, not detection. mumei is deterministic, so one run is enough; a block comes with a counterexample and a pass with a proof certificate.
- **mumei + LLM port** is the gate without hand-written ports. The LLM only writes the `.mm` body of the changed function; mumei decides. A regression let through here is a translation that dropped the defect, a flaky case is a port that differs between runs. Output-equivalence evidence reports fixed-side output differences in `GO01-D04`, `PY02-D08`, `RS01-D06`, `SOL03-D08`, `TS03-D03`; exact fixed-reference copies and adjudicated abstraction-boundary controls are pinned as negative controls, so these rows should not be read as correct-port overblocking without case review.
- **LLM review** answers holds/violated itself. A pass is the model's opinion, not a proof, and the same change can get a different answer on another run.

Flaky under mumei + LLM port: `PY02-D05`, `PY04-D11`, `RS01-D06`, `RS01-D12`, `SOL01-D03`, `SOL03-D07`, `SOL03-D08`, `TS01-D03`, `TS01-D07`, `TS02-D11`.

Flaky under LLM review: `GO02-D03`, `GO03-D06`, `GO03-D07`, `PY03-D05`, `RS03-D08`, `TS01-D12`.

## Beyond the planted defect

[MUTATION.md](MUTATION.md) makes first-order mutants of the fixed ports (relational, logical, arithmetic and constant changes) and verifies them under the pinned contracts. mumei blocks 154 of 341 scored mutants (45%); 187 pass, either because the contract does not constrain that part of the body or because the mutant is equivalent. 0 do not verify either way: 0 unsupported, 0 residual inconclusive, 0 environment failure and 0 budget exhaustion. A pinned contract only gates what it states: the planted-defect rows above are an upper bound for an arbitrary later change.
